text:
lee: seeing a spike in 5xxs and high p95 for /v1/generate in us-west-2, looks like traffic is getting routed to a slow model variant. Can we flip a bypass header quickly?

maria: on it. are we sure it's the variant and not an upstream health flake? logs show healthy pods but long tail latency.

alex: if it's variant-specific we can short-circuit routing using X-Route-Mode: fast-path -> forces routing to golden variant. low-risk and quick.

sam: note: the gateway rule priorities are weird today. last time an emergency header was added it matched too broadly. need exact host + prefix + header match.

jay: agree. suggest rule: host == "api.redwood.ai" && path_prefix == "/v1/" && header[X-Bypass] == "golden" -> route pool "golden-v1". TTL on the rule = 10m.

lee: please paste the exact nginx/edge-config snippet we can push. also who will own rollback?

maria: snippet below — plan: push as canary, monitor 2m, then scale to 100% if error rate drops. rollback if >1% 5xx or p95 > 800ms.

alex: ```
# edge-routing rule
- match:
    host: "api.redwood.ai"
    path_prefix: "/v1/"
    headers:
      X-Bypass: "golden"
  action:
    route: "pool://golden-v1"
  metadata:
    emergency: true
    ttl: 600  # seconds
```

sam: add explicit priority: 1000 so it beats the heuristic matcher. and add a metrics tag so console shows route hits.

jay: can we avoid touching existing weight configs? just add this header-only override. operators can inject header via ingress shim.

oncall-mike: I'm on pager, will watch SLO dashboard and logs. if deploy-bot triggers, I'll be ready to flip off.

maria: small operational checklist: 1) create rule in staging, 2) dry-run with header set, 3) push as canary to 5% of ingress (header-based test), 4) bump to 100% after 2m if stable, 5) set automatic rollback threshold.

lee: deploy-bot, run the canary for rule 1763201120 and notify channel when live.

deploy-bot: starting canary deploy: rule=1763201120, target=header:X-Bypass=golden, mode=canary(5%), owner=maria. Will post status updates. :rocket:

infra-bot: Dry-run passed (header match only). No config conflicts.

maria: canary live. sending test traffic now.

oncall-mike: p50/p95 improving already. 5xx rate down from 1.8% -> 0.2% for the subset.

lee: ok bump to 100% for header traffic only. continue monitoring.

maria: bumped. console: route_hits tag=golden-bypass showing expected counts.

sam: reminder — make sure traffic shaping policy doesn't persist after TTL. set rule removal scheduled for 10m from now unless we extend manually.

jay: i've added an automation to expire the rule after ttl and create a reminder in #incidents to either extend or bake permanent change.

oncall-mike: alerting thresholds verified. if anything regresses I'll flip off and post reason.

lee: good work. after stabilization let's open a short RFC for a safer permanent bypass mechanism and record the rollback playbook.

maria: will write postmortem + bake into ops runbook. tagging @product for visibility. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: canary promoted -> 100%. rule scheduled to expire at +10m unless extended.

infra-bot: rule 1763201120 created with priority=1000, ttl=600s, metrics_tag=golden-bypass.

jay: we should also add a guard in console UI to prevent accidental broad header matches (UX follow-up).

lee: agreed. closing thread when TTL expires and no issues. thanks everyone.
